comparison: Perfect agreement on methodology claims (C1, C110, C111). Both evaluations find the experimental approach, animal model, sample sizes, and ethical approval well-documented and appropriate. OpenEval and peer reviewers both praise the technical execution and rigor.

Perfect agreement on sensory-evoked response findings (C21-C27). Both evaluations support the claims about altered sensory responses and functional remapping after stroke. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'compelling evidence' for these spatially restricted deficits.

Strong agreement on behavioral deficit claims (C28-C33). OpenEval addresses C28-C33 while peer review includes C34 as well. Both find the behavioral data well-supported and consistent with the stroke model, with peer reviewers emphasizing novel insights regarding neural activity patterns.

Partial overlap on behavioral claims. OpenEval R4 addresses only C34 (discrepancy with previous research), which peer review R3 includes alongside C28-C33. Both evaluations support the claims but OpenEval specifically notes the discrepancy warrants further investigation.

Strong agreement on firing rate and behavioral correlation claims (C35-C39). OpenEval focuses on C35-C39 while peer review R4 also includes C40-C41. Both evaluations emphasize the strong correlation between peri-infarct firing rate and behavioral performance as compelling evidence.

Partial overlap on literature contextualization (C40-C41). OpenEval R6 addresses only C40-C41 while peer review R4 covers C35-C41. Both support the authors' contextualization of findings within existing literature.

Perfect agreement on functional connectivity claims (C42-C50). Both evaluations support the findings of spatially restricted deficits in functional connectivity. Peer reviewers emphasize the compelling evidence for deficits within <750 microns of the infarct.

Perfect agreement on neural assembly reorganization claims (C51-C56). Both evaluations support these novel findings about assembly reorganization after stroke. Peer reviewers note the rigorous analytic tools led to novel insights.

Perfect agreement on assembly correlation claims (C57-C60). Both evaluations support the findings of increased correlation between assemblies suggesting reduced functional specificity. Peer reviewers emphasize the rigor of the analytic approach.

Perfect agreement on assembly-movement relationship claims (C61-C62). Both evaluations support the finding that the relationship between assemblies and movement remains relatively preserved despite altered assembly structure.

Partial agreement on awake vs. anesthetized preparation claims (C75-C80). OpenEval R11 addresses C75-C80 while peer review R10 covers C75, C78-C80, C84, C109. Both support the interpretation about differences between awake and anesthetized preparations, with peer reviewers emphasizing this sheds light on discrepancies across studies.

Partial overlap on spatial specificity mechanisms (C81-C85, C72-C74). OpenEval rates C81-C85 as UNCERTAIN (speculative mechanisms), while peer review R14 supports C72-C74, C82-C83, C85. Peer reviewers found conclusions justified, while OpenEval notes mechanistic explanations require additional validation.

Minimal overlap on spatial specificity (C84). OpenEval R12 addresses C81-C85 as UNCERTAIN while peer review R10 includes C84 among SUPPORTED claims. This represents a subtle difference in evaluation of speculative mechanisms.

Minimal overlap on spatial specificity (C81). OpenEval R12 rates C81-C85 as UNCERTAIN while peer review R9 includes C81 among SUPPORTED main conclusions. OpenEval is more cautious about mechanistic interpretations.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C2-C4, C105-C108). OpenEval R13 addresses C2-C4, C105-C109 while peer review R9 covers C2-C4, C76-C77, C81, C105-C108. Both strongly support the main conclusions as well-supported by comprehensive data. Peer reviewers emphasize this is an 'important study' with 'compelling evidence.'
Minimal overlap on conclusions (C109). OpenEval R13 includes C109 in main conclusions while peer review R10 includes it with awake imaging claims. Both support the claim.

Perfect agreement on cortical excitability literature review (C5-C13). Both evaluations support these background claims as accurately summarizing existing literature. Peer reviewers note the study helps resolve contradictory findings.

Perfect agreement on awake imaging rationale (C14-C20). Both evaluations support the well-documented justification for using awake imaging. Peer reviewers emphasize this addresses discrepancies across animal studies.
Perfect agreement on post-stroke plasticity literature (C63-C71). Both evaluations support these background claims as accurately summarizing established knowledge about post-stroke plasticity.

Disagreement on mechanistic interpretation certainty (C72-C74). OpenEval rates C72-C74 as UNCERTAIN (speculative mechanisms requiring additional experiments), while peer review R14 supports C72-C74, C82-C83, C85 as justified. Peer reviewers found 'very little in the way of weaknesses' while OpenEval is more cautious about speculative claims.

Perfect agreement on study limitations (C86-C89). Both evaluations support these claims as appropriate caveats regarding cell-type specificity and age effects. Both note these are important limitations for interpreting findings.

Strong agreement on novelty and literature comparison (C90-C94). OpenEval R19 addresses C90-C94 while peer review R15 covers C90-C99. Both support the contextualization of the study's novelty and comparison to existing literature.

Partial overlap on neural assembly background (C95-C99). OpenEval R20 addresses C95-C104 rating some as UNCERTAIN, while peer review R15 covers C90-C99 as SUPPORTED. Both support the theoretical background on assemblies.

Disagreement on speculative interpretations (C100-C104). OpenEval rates C100, C103-C104 as UNCERTAIN (speculative functional consequences lacking direct experimental support), while peer review R16 supports C100-C104. Peer reviewers found 'very little in the way of weaknesses' while OpenEval identifies lack of direct experimental support for functional interpretations.

Minimal overlap on awake imaging claims (C76-C77). OpenEval R11 addresses C75-C80 while peer review R9 includes C76-C77 among main conclusions. Both support these claims about differences from anesthetized preparations.
